DETAILED ACTION
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 102
The following is a quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for the rejections under this section made in this Office action:
A person shall be entitled to a patent unless –
(a)(1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, or in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
(a)(2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
Claims 1-2, 4, 6, 8, 11, 13-14, 16-17, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by Foutch (US 11591967).
Regarding claims 1, 8, and 14, Foutch discloses a hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission for a low spool drive and a process thereof comprising: an accessory gearbox (148) in operative communication with a low speed spool motor-generator (178; “could have two modes: as an electrical generator as well as an electrical motor”); a transmission (174) in operative communication with the accessory gearbox and the low speed spool motor-generator; a low speed spool angled gearbox in operative communication with the transmission (see figures, tower shafts extend from main shafts and are at ~90 degree angles to the shafts connected to the transmission and accessory gearbox); and a low speed spool (122) in operative communication with the low speed spool angled gearbox. Foutch further discloses an engine structure proximate a compressor (114, 124) of a gas turbine engine, a low speed spool towershaft (144) coupled to the engine structure (Figures 2-3).
Regarding claim 2, Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission according to claim 1 above. Foutch further discloses the accessory gearbox is in operative communication with an oil and fuel pump (accessories 142a-c and 154; “The engine accessories 154 include a starter, fuel pump, lubricator pump, and other similar components”).
Regarding claims 4 and 13, Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission according to claims 1 and 8 above. Foutch further discloses the accessory gearbox is in operative communication with a high speed spool (120) via a high speed spool angled gearbox (see Figures, tower shafts extend from main shafts and are at ~90 degree angles to the shafts connected to the accessory gearbox).
Regarding claims 6, 11, and 16-17, Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission and process according to claims 1, 8, and 14 above. Foutch further discloses the transmission as a two speed transmission configured for hybrid electric low spool drive applications, including configuring the two-speed transmission for two operational modes (see Tables 1-2 which document multiple modes of the clutch position and different modes of operation thereof).
Regarding claim 20, Foutch discloses the process according to claim 14 above. Foutch further discloses configuring the transmission for a low spool drive power injection on ground (see Tables 1-2, operation on ground).
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in this Office action:
A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
Claims 3 and 12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Foutch (US 11591967) in view of Applicant’s Admitted Prior Art, hereinafter referenced as AAPA.
Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission for a low spool drive according to claims 1 and 8 above.
Foutch fails to teach the accessory gearbox is in operative communication with a first and second high speed spool motor-generator.
Foutch further discloses an assortment of other accessories that are connected to the high speed spool (154, 156, 158, 176).
AAPA teaches a high speed spool (N2) connected to at least two high speed spool motor generators (Figure 1, MG) in addition to the low speed spool (N1) with its own low speed spool motor generator (MG).
Because Foutch discloses multiple different accessories that are in connection to the high speed spool and the accessory gearbox, and because AAPA teaches that it is known to utilize multiple motor generators for both the low speed spool and the high speed spool, it therefore would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission for a low spool drive of Foutch such that the accessory gearbox is in operative communication with a first and second high speed spool motor-generator as taught by AAPA for the purposes of providing power and power generation when connected to the high speed spool and thereby power can be drawn from the high speed spool for quick boosts to the low speed spool and regenerated energy from either spool to be routed to electrical systems, and load sharing/redundancy/reliability. Additionally, during takeoff or climb, the high speed spool provides improved thrust, whereas for descent or landing energy can be recovered form the low speed spool.
Claims 5, 10, and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Foutch (US 11591967) in view of Joensson (WO 2008082335).
Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission and process according to claims 1, 8, and 14.
Foutch fails to teach the transmission and low speed spool angled gearbox are integrally formed sharing a common housing.
Joensson teaches a transmission mechanism for a gas turbine engine with a low speed tower shaft (19) that is connected by an angled gearbox (27) and connected to a clutch mechanism (23, 24). In Figure 2, there is a common housing, and in Figure 3 there is separate but adjacent housing. It is therefore established that utilizing a common housing or adjacent separate housing are obvious variants of one another. Utilizing a common housing can lead to reduction in parts and weight.
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission and process of Foutch such that the transmission and low speed spool angled gearbox are integrally formed sharing a common housing as taught by Joensson for the purposes of reducing parts and weight through a common housing.
Claims 7, 9, and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Foutch (US 11591967).
Regarding claims 7 and 9;
Foutch discloses the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission according to claims 1 and 8 above.
Foutch fails to teach the transmission is bolted to the accessory gearbox configured as a line removable unit.
Foutch discloses another clutch mechanism (150) is a stand-alone unit that is attached to the accessory gearbox (e.g., with bolts). The transmission mechanism of Foutch (174) is external to the accessory gearbox and arranged adjacent thereof.
Because Foutch discloses a clutch mechanism that is attached to the accessory gearbox with bolts, and because Foutch discloses the transmission mechanism is external to the accessory gearbox and arranged adjacent thereof, it therefore would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the hybrid electric gas turbine engine two speed transmission of Foutch such that the transmission mechanism is bolted to the accessory gearbox as taught by Foutch for the purposes of enabling easier maintenance to be performed as the transmission is externally attached (via bolts).
Regarding claim 19;
Foutch discloses the process according to claim 14 above. Foutch further discloses utilizing the low spool drive for generating power as the motor is configured as a motor-generator.
Foutch fails to teach the power extraction is arranged for AC loads and battery recharge.
When utilizing a motor generator with a low speed spool, the spool is connected to the fan and allows for high rotational inertia and providing a stable source of energy, less prone to rapid RPM fluctuations making it ideal for steady energy extraction during idle and descent. The low speed spool operates at lower RPMs and leads to lower AC frequencies. The low speed spool can be dedicated to powering les demanding AC loads during cruise, and battery recharge can be supported during descent. In sum, high inertia provides steady energy during descent/low thrust, reduces load on high speed spool and preserving engine efficiency, leverages the rotational energy for charging the generator (which can recharge a battery), and provide AC critical loads with variable frequency. It therefore would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the process of Foutch such that the power extraction is arranged for AC loads and battery recharge for the purposes of providing steady energy during descent or low thrust and preserving energy efficiency and to charge the battery for backup power in the event of failure and/or load sharing.
Claim 18 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Foutch (US 11591967) in view of Muldoon (US 10563591).
Foutch discloses the process according to claim 14 above. Foutch further discloses multiple operational modes with respect to the low spool motor-generator drive including for high speed operation (Tables 1-2, open/closed clutch position which determines direct drive operation of the motor-generator), and further provides for low speed spool operation selecting from the group of ground idle speed and flight idle speed (Tables 1-2).
Foutch fails to teach the mode 2 is configured to provide up to a 3x increase in motor shaft speed wherein the transmission includes a gear ratio of 3.0.
Muldoon teaches a low spool tower shaft (94) connected to an accessory gearbox (70) through a transmission mechanism (104) which has a variable speed transmission through a series of gears. Muldoon teaches “The rotational speed of inner shaft 40 and thus the rotational speed of low spool transmission 74 may vary over a large range of speeds during operation of gas turbine engine 20. For example, the rotational speed of lower lay shaft 96 may range from between approximately 20% and 100% of a maximum rotation speed experienced during take-off. As used in this context only, “approximately” means ±5%. Variable speed transmission 104 may comprise gears of varying gear ratios. In this regard, variable speed transmission 104 may be configured to adjust its gear ratio in response to an increase or decrease in the rotation speed of lower lay shaft 96, thereby keeping the rotational speed of output 106 at a generally constant speed. As used herein only, a “generally constant speed” means ±10% variation in rotation speed.”
It would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to modify the process of Foutch such that the mode 2 is configured to provide up to a 3x increase in motor shaft speed wherein the transmission includes a gear ratio of 3.0 as taught by Muldoon as the utilization of a gear ratio to change the speeds of operation is known for the purposes of optimizing the accessory performance to boost speeds at low spool RPM, ensures sufficient power delivery to accessories during idle (when spool speed is minimal), optimizing in flight efficiency (maintains functionality at flight idle or low thrust phases), and reduces weight to allow for smaller and lighter accessories with higher speeds via the gear ratio.
Conclusion
The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure.
Edwards (US 9938850), Mackin (US 10336461), and Foutch (US 11333077) each disclose various spool and accessory gearbox arrangements.
Conclusion
